label: prop:collatz-contact-boundary
title: The $[2]_q$-contact boundary on the Reeb bundle
html:
Proposition. The [2]_q-contact boundary on the Reeb bundle

Proposition (within a QOU with 2 \mid \chi(A); conditional on conj:q-collatz; "[2]_q-contact boundary"). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q whose Frobenius–Hopf object satisfies 2 \mid \chi(A) — for instance the Descartes universe, \chi(A) = -6 — and let \mathcal{R}_p = (S^3 \xrightarrow{\pi_H} S^2, \xi_q) be its Reeb bundle (Reeb bundle) with U(1) fiber parametrized by q = e^{i\varTheta}. The parity 2 \mid \chi(A) is what makes the [2]_q-divisor Kummer-removable below; \chi(A) = -6 is a property of the Descartes universe, not of a general QOU. The q-Collatz orbit of P \in \mathcal{S}(q)_{>0} converges if and only if its orbit contact average (Collatz contact boundary) attains the threshold \langle v_{[2]} \rangle(P) \geq 2. Equivalently, the q-Collatz conjecture is the contact condition

\bigl\langle v_{[2]}([3]_q P + 1) \bigr\rangle \geq 2 \quad\text{for all } P \in \mathcal{S}(q)_{>0}.

Proof. Since 1 < v^*(q) < 2 (we have [2]_q < [3]_q < [2]_q^2), the orbit converges whenever each tripling is followed by at least two halvings on average, i.e., \langle v_{[2]} \rangle(P) \geq 2.

Two halvings multiply by [2]_q^{-2}; one tripling multiplies by [3]_q / [2]_q. The net factor per cycle is

\frac{[3]_q}{[2]_q} \cdot \frac{1}{[2]_q^2} = \frac{[3]_q}{[2]_q^3}.

This is contractive because [3]_q < [2]_q^2 < [2]_q^3. The contraction ratio is

\frac{[3]_q}{[2]_q^3} = \frac{[2]_q^2 - q}{[2]_q^3} = \frac{1}{[2]_q} - \frac{q}{[2]_q^3}.

The orbit shrinks by slightly more than 1/[2]_q per cycle. The margin between two halvings and the minimum needed is

[2]_q^2 - [3]_q = q.

Since q is positive, the per-cycle factor is strictly contractive and the threshold \langle v_{[2]} \rangle \geq 2 is sufficient for convergence.

The sharp threshold is v^* = \log [3]_q / \log [2]_q. Since v^* < 2 is proved algebraically, the integer condition \langle v_{[2]} \rangle \geq 2 avoids transcendental quantities.

At q = 1, the average 2-adic valuation of 3n+1 for odd n is exactly 2 (from \Pr(v_2(3n+1) = k) = 2^{-k}). This provides exactly two halvings per tripling, meeting the threshold.
